questions.stem: What is a useful organizational purpose of an exit interview with a departing nurse?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Assign responsibility for unresolved unit problems to the departing nurse after the resignation is final","B":"Collect candid feedback about the work experience and reasons for leaving to identify improvement opportunities","C":"Prevent the employee from leaving by requiring withdrawal of the resignation during the interview","D":"Replace retention analysis because one exit interview is sufficient to explain all staff turnover patterns"}}
questions.rationale: Exit interviews can collect feedback about why employees leave and reveal workplace, management, training, culture, or retention issues. Organizations should analyze the information as one input for improvement rather than treating it as proof of a single cause.
questions.source_name: SHRM — What Can Exit Interviews Teach Us About Employee Retention?
questions.source_detail: Current SHRM discussion accessed 2026-08-14: exit interviews gather information about why employees leave and can inform retention and organizational improvement efforts.

questions.stem: After a fall, an older adult has severe hip pain, cannot bear weight, and the affected leg appears shortened and externally rotated. What should the nurse suspect?

questions.rationale: Hip fracture should be strongly suspected after a fall when there is hip/groin pain, inability to bear weight, and characteristic deformity such as shortening and external rotation. Imaging is required to confirm the diagnosis.

questions.stem: A client has leg pain and numbness that worsen with standing or walking and improve with sitting or leaning forward. Which disorder best fits this pattern?

questions.rationale: Neurogenic claudication from lumbar spinal stenosis commonly worsens with standing or lumbar extension and improves with sitting or forward flexion. The positional pattern helps distinguish it from other causes of leg discomfort.

questions.stem: A client has low-back pain radiating down one leg with numbness and tingling in a nerve-root distribution. Which condition is most consistent?

questions.rationale: Sciatica is a clinical pattern of radicular pain that may include numbness, tingling, or weakness along the affected nerve distribution. Lumbar disc herniation is a common cause of nerve-root compression or inflammation.

questions.stem: After head trauma, a client briefly loses consciousness, becomes alert, then rapidly deteriorates neurologically. Which injury is classically associated with this lucid-interval pattern?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Uncomplicated concussion, because rapid deterioration after a lucid interval is expected and benign","B":"Chronic subdural hematoma, which always produces the same brief lucid interval after a head injury","C":"Epidural hematoma, often involving traumatic injury to the middle meningeal artery after skull trauma","D":"Ischemic stroke, because a traumatic lucid interval specifically indicates cerebral arterial embolism"}}
questions.rationale: A lucid interval after traumatic loss of consciousness followed by neurologic deterioration is classically associated with epidural hematoma, often from middle meningeal arterial injury. The pattern is not present in every epidural hematoma and is not pathognomonic.
questions.source_detail: History and Physical: classic lucid interval; etiology commonly middle meningeal artery after blunt trauma; last update July 7, 2025; accessed 2026-08-14.
